title: Banach-Space Differential Calculus and Banach Manifolds

items.title: Fréchet derivative between Banach spaces
items.statement: Let U be open in a real Banach space X and f:U→Y map to a real Banach space Y. The Fréchet derivative of f at x∈U is a bounded linear map Df(x):X→Y such that ||f(x+h)-f(x)-Df(x)h||/||h||→0 as h→0 with x+h∈U.
items.strategy: Fix the real-scalar convention for this manifold page, formulate the remainder as o(||h||), and prove directly that differentiability implies continuity. Do not substitute directional or Gâteaux differentiability.
items.axiom_audit: ZF relative to the stated Banach spaces.

references.title: Zuoqin Wang, Lecture 6: Differential Calculus on Banach Spaces — §2.1

items.title: The Fréchet derivative is unique
items.statement: If two bounded linear maps A,B:X→Y both satisfy the Fréchet remainder condition for f at x, then A=B.
items.strategy: For v≠0 insert h=tv, divide the difference of the two remainder estimates by |t|, and let t→0 to obtain (A-B)v=0; handle v=0 by linearity.
items.axiom_audit: ZF; a single explicit scalar sequence suffices.

items.title: Chain sum product and composition rules for Banach derivatives
items.statement: Fréchet derivatives satisfy linearity, the bounded-bilinear product rule D(B(f,g))h=B(Df h,g)+B(f,Dg h), and the chain rule D(g∘f)(x)=Dg(f(x))Df(x), whenever the displayed maps and open domains are defined.
items.strategy: Write each increment as its linear part plus an o(||h||) remainder. Boundedness controls sums and compositions. For the bilinear rule expand B(f+Δf,g+Δg), and bound the cross term by bounded bilinearity and the local O(||h||) estimates supplied by differentiability.
items.axiom_audit: ZF; all estimates are finite and local.

items.title: C k map between Banach spaces
items.statement: For open U⊂X, f:U→Y is C^1 when it is Fréchet differentiable and x↦Df(x) is continuous in operator norm. Inductively it is C^k when D^{k-1}f is Fréchet differentiable as a map to bounded (k-1)-linear maps and D^k f is operator-norm continuous; C^0 means continuous and C^∞ means C^k for every k.
items.strategy: Use the joint operator norm on bounded multilinear maps, identify iterated derivatives with such maps, and state the recursive convention. Do not use merely pointwise continuity of derivatives.
items.axiom_audit: ZF relative to the stated operator spaces.

items.title: Banach mean value estimate on a convex set
items.statement: Assume AC. If U is open and convex in a real Banach space X, f:U→Y is Fréchet differentiable, and ||Df(z)||≤M on [x,y]⊂U, then ||f(y)-f(x)||≤M||y-x||.
items.strategy: Put w=f(y)-f(x). If w=0 the claim is immediate. Otherwise the Hahn–Banach norming theorem gives φ∈Y* with ||φ||=1 and φ(w)=||w||. The scalar function t↦φ(f(x+t(y-x))) is continuous on [0,1], differentiable on (0,1), and has derivative φ(Df(x+t(y-x))(y-x)). Apply the scalar mean-value theorem and bound that derivative by M||y-x||. This needs neither a Banach-valued integral nor continuity of Df.
items.axiom_audit: Full AC is used exactly through Hahn–Banach dual norming; no further choice occurs.

items.title: Inverse function theorem for Banach spaces
items.statement: Assume AC. Let f:U⊂X→Y be C^k, k≥1, between real Banach spaces. If Df(a) is a bounded linear isomorphism, then f restricts on neighbourhoods of a and f(a) to a C^k diffeomorphism, with D(f^{-1})(f(x))=Df(x)^{-1}.
items.strategy: Translate and conjugate by Df(a)^{-1} to normalize a=f(a)=0 and Df(0)=I. Shrink a ball so ||Df-I||≤q<1. For small y, x↦y-(f(x)-x) is a contraction of a closed ball, giving a unique solution; the same mean-value estimate makes the inverse Lipschitz. Comparing f(x+h)-f(x) with Df(x)h proves differentiability of the inverse, with derivative Df(x)^{-1}. Neumann perturbation keeps Df invertible. Finally prove locally from the Neumann series that inversion on bounded isomorphisms is C∞ with derivative H↦-A^{-1}HA^{-1}; the derivative formula and the chain rule then induct on k.
items.axiom_audit: Full AC is propagated from the mean-value estimate's Hahn–Banach step; contraction iteration makes no new arbitrary choice.

items.title: Implicit function theorem for Banach spaces
items.statement: Assume AC. Let F:U⊂X×Y→Z be C^k, k≥1, with F(a,b)=0 and D_YF(a,b):Y→Z a bounded linear isomorphism. Locally F(x,y)=0 exactly when y=g(x) for a unique C^k map g, and Dg=-(D_YF)^{-1}D_XF along the graph.
items.strategy: Apply the inverse theorem to Φ(x,y)=(x,F(x,y)); its block derivative has an explicit triangular inverse. Write Φ^{-1}(x,z)=(x,h(x,z)), set g(x)=h(x,0), and differentiate F(x,g(x))=0 to obtain the derivative formula.
items.axiom_audit: Full AC is inherited from the Banach inverse theorem; block algebra adds no choice.

items.title: Countable base Banach manifold and smooth map
items.statement: A C^k Banach manifold is a Hausdorff second-countable space equipped with a specified atlas of charts into a fixed real Banach space, with C^k transition maps in the Fréchet sense. A chart of the structured manifold means a member of that atlas. A map is C^k when all representatives in the specified source and target atlases are C^k; smooth means C^∞.
items.strategy: Specify the Hausdorff and countable-base assumptions, distinguish an arbitrary local homeomorphism on the underlying space from a chart in the chosen manifold atlas, and define smoothness through representatives in those atlases; independence among the atlas charts follows from their transition compatibility and the chain rule.
items.axiom_audit: Definition; no atlas selection or new choice is asserted.

references.title: Alberto Abbondandolo and Pietro Majer, Lectures on the Morse Complex — §2.1

items.title: Tangent space and differential on a Banach manifold
items.statement: For p in a Banach manifold M, T_pM is the space of chart-coordinate velocities modulo the transition-derivative relation. For C^1 f:M→N, Df(p) is represented in charts by the Fréchet derivative of the coordinate representative.
items.strategy: Define tangent vectors as classes (φ,v), with (φ,v)~(ψ,D(ψ∘φ^{-1})(φ(p))v), then define Df by chart representatives. Defer well-definedness and functoriality to the following lemma.
items.axiom_audit: Definition; no new choice.

references.title: Abbondandolo–Majer, Lectures on the Morse Complex — §2.1

items.title: Banach manifold differentials are chart independent
items.statement: The tangent equivalence relation and differential above are well defined. Moreover D(g∘f)=Dg∘Df and D(id)=id.
items.strategy: Use the chain rule on triple coordinate changes to prove transitivity and on changed source/target charts to prove conjugacy of coordinate formulas. Differentiate transition-map identities to see transition derivatives are inverse. Composition and identity then follow in one chart.
items.axiom_audit: ZF relative to the chart data; no inverse theorem or choice is required because transition maps already have differentiable inverses.

references.title: Abbondandolo–Majer, Lectures on the Morse Complex — §2.1

items.title: Split Banach submanifold
items.statement: S⊂M is a split C^k submanifold when near each p∈S a chart into a Banach decomposition E=E_0⊕E_1 by closed complemented subspaces sends S exactly to the slice E_0×{0}. Then T_pS is complemented in T_pM.
items.strategy: Build splitness into the chart definition and record the induced tangent inclusion componentwise. On overlaps the local model spaces are linearly isomorphic, so each connected component has one model type; do not claim that distinct components share a model or that an arbitrary closed linear subspace is a Banach submanifold.
items.axiom_audit: Definition; a complement is part of the local data.

references.title: Abbondandolo–Majer, Lectures on the Morse Complex — §2.1

items.title: Regular value theorem for Banach manifolds
items.statement: Assume AC. If f:M→N is C^k and for every p∈f^{-1}(q), Df(p) is onto with complemented kernel, then f^{-1}(q) is a split C^k submanifold and T_p f^{-1}(q)=ker Df(p).
items.strategy: In charts split X=ker L⊕X_1 for L=Df(p). Surjectivity makes L|X_1 bijective, and bounded inverse makes its inverse bounded. Apply the implicit theorem in X_1, express the level set as a graph over ker L, straighten it, and differentiate to identify the tangent.
items.axiom_audit: Full AC is inherited from the implicit/bounded inverse route. No complement is chosen: split kernel is an explicit hypothesis.

references.title: Abbondandolo–Majer, Lectures on the Morse Complex — §2.2, regular values

items.title: Smooth Banach vector bundle and section
items.statement: A smooth Banach vector bundle π:E→M with second-countable Banach fibre F is locally smoothly trivial as U×F with fibrewise bounded-linear transition maps depending smoothly on the base. A smooth section is smooth s:M→E with πs=id; locally it is a smooth F-valued map. At a zero p of a section, its vertical derivative D^v s(p):T_pM→E_p is the derivative of that fibre component, transported back to the fibre; this is independent of the trivialization.
items.strategy: State local trivializations and their bounded-linear cocycle, then define sections. At a zero, define the vertical derivative as the derivative of the fibre component and show transition-derivative terms vanish there.
items.axiom_audit: Definition; no new choice.

references.title: Abbondandolo–Majer, Lectures on the Morse Complex — Banach-bundle sections in §2

items.title: A transverse Banach bundle section has a split zero submanifold
items.statement: Assume AC. If a smooth section s is transverse to the zero section—at every zero its vertical derivative is onto with complemented kernel—then s^{-1}(0) is split smooth and T_p s^{-1}(0)=ker D^v s(p).
items.strategy: In a local trivialization at a zero, represent s by σ:U→F and apply the regular-value theorem to σ^{-1}(0). Under another trivialization Dσ at a zero is multiplied by a bounded fibre isomorphism, proving the condition and tangent description intrinsic.
items.axiom_audit: Full AC is propagated from the regular-value theorem; local trivialization is supplied data.

references.title: Abbondandolo–Majer, Lectures on the Morse Complex — regular sections in §2

items.title: Fredholm map between Banach manifolds
items.statement: A C^1 map f:M→N is Fredholm when Df(p) is Fredholm for every p. Its index at p is ind Df(p); the map has index n when this integer is constantly n.
items.strategy: Coordinate changes conjugate Df(p) by bounded isomorphisms, preserving finite kernel/cokernel, closed range, and index. Keep pointwise index separate from the following local-constancy result.
items.axiom_audit: No new choice; any choice used by later splitting results is not part of this definition.

references.title: Abbondandolo–Majer, Lectures on the Morse Complex — §2.2

items.title: Local finite-dimensional reduction for a Fredholm map
items.statement: Assume AC. After choosing centred charts at p and f(p), let L be the derivative of the chart representative and fix splittings E=ker L plus E_1 and F=ran L plus C. Near p the map is smoothly equivalent to (u,v)↦(u,g(u,v)), with v in the finite-dimensional kernel and g valued in the fixed finite-dimensional complement C.
items.strategy: Use supplied splittings X=N⊕X_1 and Y=R⊕C. In charts, the derivative of the R-component restricted to X_1 is an isomorphism. Apply inverse/implicit theory to replace X_1 by that component. The residual C-map has finite-dimensional kernel variable N and obstruction target C; retain its dependence on the solved coordinate and make no constant-rank claim.
items.axiom_audit: Full AC is used exactly through Fredholm splitting and the implicit theorem.

references.title: Abbondandolo–Majer, Lectures on the Morse Complex — §2.2 and Theorem 2.19 proof

items.title: The index of a Fredholm map is locally constant
items.statement: Assume AC. For a C^1 Fredholm map, p↦ind Df(p) is locally constant and hence constant on each connected component.
items.strategy: In fixed charts p↦Df(p) is operator-norm continuous by C^1. Apply openness and local constancy of the Fredholm-operator index. Chart changes preserve index, and an integer-valued locally constant function is constant on connected components.
items.axiom_audit: Full AC is propagated from the operator-level Fredholm theorem.

references.title: Abbondandolo–Majer, Lectures on the Morse Complex — §2.2

items.title: Surjectivity alone does not imply a complemented kernel
items.statement: At the Banach-space linear level, surjectivity does not imply that the kernel is complemented, equivalently that a bounded linear right inverse exists. The c_0 in ell-infinity witness is not a Banach-manifold counterexample under the library's second-countability convention. Finite-dimensional and Fredholm kernels are automatically complemented.
items.strategy: Contrast exact split-kernel hypotheses with mere surjectivity, quote the bounded-right-inverse equivalence, and identify finite-dimensional/Fredholm kernels as the automatic safe case. Mention the companion counterexample without depending on it.
items.axiom_audit: Full AC is inherited from regular values; the right-inverse equivalence itself assumes DC.

references.title: Abbondandolo–Majer, Lectures on the Morse Complex — §2.2

title: Banach-Space Differential Calculus and Banach Manifolds: Examples

items.title: The derivative of a bounded bilinear map
items.statement: For bounded bilinear B:X×Y→Z, DB(x,y)(h,k)=B(h,y)+B(x,k). Thus Banach-algebra multiplication has Dm(a,b)(h,k)=hb+ak and x↦B(x,x) has derivative h↦B(h,x)+B(x,h).
items.strategy: Expand B(x+h,y+k)-B(x,y). The proposed linear part leaves B(h,k), bounded by C||h||||k||=o(||(h,k)||). Specialize to multiplication and the diagonal.
items.axiom_audit: ZF; finite bilinear estimates only.

items.title: The Banach inverse theorem for a small Lipschitz perturbation of the identity
items.statement: Assume AC. If X is Banach and g:X→X is Lipschitz with q<1, F=I+g is bijective and F^{-1} is Lipschitz with constant at most (1-q)^{-1}. If g is C^k, then F is a global C^k diffeomorphism.
items.strategy: For y solve x=y-g(x) by fixed point. Subtract two equations for the inverse estimate. If g is C^k, difference quotients give ||Dg||≤q, so I+Dg is Neumann-invertible; local C^k inverses agree with the global inverse.
items.axiom_audit: Full AC is propagated from the owned inverse theorem; the fixed-point construction adds none.

items.title: A regular level set in a Banach space
items.statement: Assume AC. For real Banach spaces K and Y, let X=K⊕Y be a topological direct sum. The bounded projection p:X→Y has every y as a regular value and p^{-1}(y) is an affine split submanifold with tangent K.
items.strategy: Dp=p everywhere, it is onto, and ker p=K is complemented by Y. Apply regular values and identify the fibre directly as an affine translate.
items.axiom_audit: No new choice; full AC is inherited from regular values.

references.title: Abbondandolo–Majer, Lectures on the Morse Complex — §2.2

items.title: A projection with finite-dimensional kernel is Fredholm
items.statement: Assume AC. If N and Y are real Banach spaces, dim N<∞, and X=N⊕Y is their topological direct sum, the projection p:X→Y is a smooth Fredholm map of index dim N and its local finite-dimensional reduction has zero obstruction space.
items.strategy: Dp=p, with finite kernel N, closed surjective range and zero cokernel, so ind p=dim N. The displayed coordinates already give the reduction normal form.
items.axiom_audit: Full AC is inherited from the reduction interface; the finite-dimensional computation adds none.

references.title: Abbondandolo–Majer, Lectures on the Morse Complex — §2.2

items.title: A closed uncomplemented subspace is not a split Banach submanifold
items.statement: Assuming the Axiom of Countable Choice, c_0 is closed in ℓ∞ but is not a split Banach submanifold of ℓ∞.
items.strategy: Closedness makes c_0 a Banach subspace of ℓ∞. Its tangent cone at 0 is exactly c_0: every v∈c_0 is the velocity of t↦tv, while every derivative at 0 of a curve in c_0 is a norm limit of difference quotients in the closed subspace c_0. If the inclusion were a split submanifold near 0, the split chart and its derivative would therefore make this tangent copy of c_0 complemented in ℓ∞, contradicting the published Phillips-theorem consequence.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is used exactly through the published noncomplementation theorem.

title: Compact Self Adjoint Hilbert Schmidt and Trace Class Operators

items.title: Norm of a self adjoint operator from its quadratic form
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For bounded self-adjoint T on a nonzero real or complex Hilbert space, ||T||=sup_{||x||=1}|⟨Tx,x⟩|; for the zero space both sides are defined as zero.
items.strategy: Cauchy–Schwarz gives the easy inequality. If M bounds q(x)=⟨Tx,x⟩, first multiply y by a unit scalar in the complex case so that ⟨Tx,y⟩ is real and nonnegative. Real polarization applied to tx and t^{-1}y gives |⟨Tx,y⟩|≤(M/2)(t²||x||²+t^{-2}||y||²); choosing t²=||y||/||x|| yields |⟨Tx,y⟩|≤M||x||||y||. Handle zero vectors separately and take the supremum over unit y. This proves the exact constant in both scalar fields and includes the zero Hilbert space convention.
items.axiom_audit: Only AC_omega inherited from the Hilbert-adjoint interface; no new choice.

references.title: Gerald Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis — §1.3, Problems 1.19–1.20 (polarization and quadratic-form bounds)
Anthony W. Knapp, Advanced Real Analysis — Chapter II, §2, Proposition 2.2

items.title: Norm point of a compact self adjoint operator is an eigenvalue up to sign
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If T is a nonzero compact self-adjoint operator, then either ||T|| or -||T|| is an eigenvalue with a unit eigenvector.
items.strategy: Use AC_omega for unit x_n with |⟨Tx_n,x_n⟩|>||T||-1/n and pass to an infinite subsequence on which one sign occurs, choosing its least successive indices. For λ=±||T||, expand ||(T-λI)x_n||² and use ||Tx_n||≤||T|| to get convergence to zero. The compact closure of T of the unit ball is sequentially compact by the choice-free compactness implication, so a subsequence Tx_{n_j} converges; λ≠0 then makes x_{n_j} converge to a unit eigenvector.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is used exactly to choose the approximate maximizers. Subsequences are selected by least indices, and compactness implies sequential compactness in ZF; no DC or full AC is used.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp — Chapter II, §2, Theorem 2.3 proof

items.title: Eigenspaces of a self adjoint operator are orthogonal
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Every eigenvalue of a self-adjoint operator is real, and eigenspaces for distinct eigenvalues are orthogonal.
items.strategy: For Tx=λx compare ⟨Tx,x⟩ with its conjugate to get λ real. If Ty=μy, self-adjointness gives λ⟨x,y⟩=μ⟨x,y⟩ in the first-variable-linear convention, so distinct eigenvalues force orthogonality.
items.axiom_audit: Only inherited AC_omega from the adjoint interface; no new choice.

items.title: Orthogonal complement of an eigenspace is invariant
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If T is self-adjoint and E_λ=ker(T-λI), then E_λ and E_λ^⊥ are closed T-invariant subspaces, and the restrictions of T to them are self-adjoint.
items.strategy: E_λ is a closed kernel. For x∈E_λ^⊥ and y∈E_λ, ⟨Tx,y⟩=⟨x,Ty⟩=λ⟨x,y⟩=0. Restrict the adjoint identity to each invariant orthogonal summand.
items.axiom_audit: Only inherited AC_omega from the adjoint interface; no choice.

items.title: Spectral theorem for compact self adjoint operators
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For compact self-adjoint T on a real or complex Hilbert space, its nonzero eigenvalues form a finite or countable set of real numbers, have finite multiplicity, and can accumulate only at 0. Their orthogonal eigenspaces have closed span (ker T)^⊥=closure(ran T), and Tx=Σ_{λ≠0}λP_λx in norm. On a complex Hilbert space these eigenvalues are exactly the nonzero spectrum. No basis of ker T is selected.
items.strategy: For λ≠0 the unit ball of E_λ, scaled by λ, is a closed subset of the compact closure of T(B), so compactness of the unit ball makes E_λ finite-dimensional. Compactness also gives total boundedness: infinitely many distinct eigenvalues with modulus at least ε would, using only finite choice for each finite subfamily, produce arbitrarily large ε-separated finite subsets of T(B), impossible for a fixed finite ε/3-net. Hence the nonzero eigenvalues form a countable union of finite sets; AC_omega enumerates them and chooses finite ON bases. Let M be their closed span. If T were nonzero on M^⊥, its compact self-adjoint restriction would have a norm eigenvector, contradicting the definition of M. Thus M^⊥=ker T; self-adjointness then gives ran T⊂M, while every nonzero eigenvector lies in ran T, so M=(ker T)^⊥=closure(ran T). Fourier expansion in M and the fact that only finitely many eigenvalues exceed each positive threshold give the displayed norm expansion and operator-norm convergence of its finite spectral truncations. In the complex case, if μ≠0 is not an eigenvalue, its positive distance from the eigenvalue set lets one define a bounded diagonal inverse to T-μI on M and the scalar inverse -μ^{-1}I on ker T; hence μ is resolvent. Never choose a basis of ker T.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is used exactly to enumerate the countable union of finite eigenvalue sets, choose their finite ON bases, and choose approximate eigenvectors. Compact-to-sequential compactness and the finite-net multiplicity arguments are ZF. No DC, full AC, or kernel basis is used.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp — Chapter II, §2, Theorem 2.3

items.title: Orthonormal eigenbasis for a compact self adjoint operator
items.statement: Assume AC. Every compact self-adjoint operator has a Hilbert basis of eigenvectors, obtained by adjoining a Hilbert basis of ker T to bases of the nonzero eigenspaces.
items.strategy: Apply Zorn directly to orthonormal subsets of ker T. Maximality forces dense span, since any nonzero orthogonal vector could be normalized and adjoined. Unite this family with the support eigenvectors. This avoids the defective planned maximal-family dependency path.
items.axiom_audit: Full AC is used exactly through Zorn to select a basis of the possibly nonseparable kernel.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp — Chapter II, §2, Theorem 2.3

items.title: Positive square root of a compact positive operator
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let H be a real or complex Hilbert space and let T be a compact self-adjoint positive operator. Then T has a compact positive square root S with S^2=T, unique among compact positive square roots, acting by sqrt(lambda) on each positive eigenspace of T and by zero on ker T.
items.strategy: Scaffold repair (Step 3b): the self-adjointness hypothesis is necessary; over a real Hilbert space a skew operator with vanishing quadratic form (a 90 degree rotation) is positive in the scaffold's sense but is not self-adjoint. Construct S by the spectral series sum sqrt(lambda) P_lambda; compactness is immediate for empty or finite positive spectrum and follows from finite-rank truncations only in the countably infinite case; uniqueness over all compact positive square roots via A=(R+R*)/2, K=(R-R*)/2 with AK=-KA.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is inherited from the support spectral theorem and compact norm closure; finite-dimensional diagonalization adds no infinite selection.

items.title: Absolute value and singular values of a compact operator
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For compact T:H→K set |T|=(T*T)^{1/2}. Its singular values are the nonzero eigenvalues of |T| in nonincreasing order with multiplicity, with zeros appended for finite rank; T=0 has the all-zero sequence.
items.strategy: The ideal property makes T*T compact and adjoint identities make it positive. Apply the square-root lemma, order its countable positive spectrum using finiteness above thresholds, and specify zero padding.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is propagated from compact square roots and the adjoint interface; ordering the already countable multiset adds no stronger choice.

items.title: Singular value decomposition for compact operators
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For compact T:H→K, index the positive singular values as (s_n) over 1≤n≤r when ran T is finite-dimensional of dimension r, over the positive integers when ran T is infinite-dimensional, and by the empty family when T=0. There are orthonormal systems (e_n) in (ker T)^⊥ and (f_n) in closure(ran T), with exactly that index set, such that Tx=Σ_ns_n⟨x,e_n⟩f_n in norm. The map Ue_n=f_n extends by zero on ker T to a partial isometry and T=U|T|. The separate singular-value sequence remains zero-padded after finite rank r.
items.strategy: Choose one support eigenvector e_n for each occurrence of a positive singular value |T|e_n=s_ne_n and set f_n=Te_n/s_n. The identity ⟨Te_i,Te_j⟩=⟨T*Te_i,e_j⟩ gives orthonormality. Show ker|T|=kerT and the f_n span closure(ranT). Fourier expansion on the support yields the series over the positive-singular-value index set; extend e_n↦f_n isometrically and vanish on kerT. For finite rank, append zeros only to the numerical singular-value sequence, not to the orthonormal systems.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is inherited from the support spectral and Fourier expansions; only countably many finite eigenspace bases are selected, and no basis of either kernel or cokernel is chosen.

items.title: Singular values equal approximation numbers
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For compact T between Hilbert spaces and a_n(T)=inf{||T-F||:rank F<n}, one has a_n(T)=s_n(T), with zero padding.
items.strategy: The SVD truncation through n-1 has rank below n and remainder norm s_n. Conversely rank F<n has a nonzero kernel vector on span{e_1,…,e_n}; normalize it and use ||Tx||≥s_n to get ||T-F||≥s_n. Cover zero and finite-rank cases by padding.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is inherited from SVD; finite rank-nullity adds no choice.

items.title: Compact operator iff approximation numbers tend to zero
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For any bounded T between Hilbert spaces, set a_0(T)=||T|| and a_n(T)=inf_{rank F<n}||T-F|| for n≥1. Then T is compact iff the resulting zero-based sequence tends to zero. For compact T, a_n(T) is the zero-padded singular value s_n(T) for every n≥1.
items.strategy: Define the harmless initial value a_0(T)=||T|| so convergence has the library's required ℕ-domain. For compact T use equality with singular values on the positive-indexed tail and their decay. Conversely use AC_omega for finite-rank F_n with ||T-F_n||≤a_n+1/n for n≥1, set F_0=0, and invoke compact-operator norm closure. Thus the iff concerns arbitrary bounded T without defining singular values circularly there.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega supplies approximate minimizers and is propagated by the norm-closure theorem; no full AC is used.

items.title: Finite rank operators are norm dense in compact Hilbert space operators
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Relabel the SVD system by positive integers and let T_n retain its first n terms, with T_0=0. Then every compact Hilbert-space operator satisfies ||T-T_n||=s_{n+1}(T) for n∈ℕ and is an operator-norm limit of finite-rank operators.
items.strategy: First relabel the infinite-rank SVD system from the library's zero-based index set to positive integers so its m-th vector corresponds to the numerical singular value s_m(T). Define a zero-based approximation sequence by taking the first n singular terms and T_0=0. Compute the remainder norm as s_{n+1}(T), which tends to zero; cover finite-rank and zero cases via zero padding.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is inherited from SVD; truncations are explicit.

items.title: Hilbert Schmidt operators form a two sided ideal
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Hilbert–Schmidt operators form a vector space, are adjoint-stable, and satisfy ||ATB||_HS≤||A||||T||_HS||B|| for bounded compatible A,B.
items.strategy: For left multiplication sum ||ATe||²≤||A||²Σ||Te||². For right multiplication apply that bound to B*T* and take adjoints. Minkowski follows from finite scalar Cauchy–Schwarz on finite basis sums, then the finite-subset supremum.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is propagated from basis independence and adjoints; no basis existence is asserted.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp — Chapter II, §5, Proposition 2.8

items.title: Trace class operator
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. A compact operator T is trace class when the zero-based shifted series Σ_{m∈N}s_{m+1}(T) converges; this sum is its trace norm ||T||_1.
items.strategy: Use the explicit zero-based shift (s_{m+1})_{m∈N} of the nonincreasing zero-padded singular sequence, include finite-rank and zero cases, and do not define trace class through a diagonal sum whose invariance is not yet proved.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is propagated from singular values; no new choice.

items.title: Trace class iff product of two Hilbert Schmidt operators
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. T on H is trace class iff T=AB for Hilbert–Schmidt B:H→K and A:K→H for some K. Moreover ||AB||_1≤||A||_HS||B||_HS, and trace-class T has a factorization attaining equality.
items.strategy: For trace-class T=U|T| apply the compact-positive square-root lemma to obtain C=|T|^{1/2}, then take B=C, A=UC; squared HS norms are Σs_n. Conversely AB is compact. For its first n singular pairs, Σs_j=Σ⟨Be_j,A*f_j⟩; finite Cauchy–Schwarz and HS bounds on orthonormal families give ≤||B||_HS||A*||_HS. Take sup n and use adjoint invariance.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is inherited from SVD and the imported Hilbert–Schmidt results. Estimating interchanges are finite.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp — Chapter II, §5, Propositions 2.8–2.9

items.title: Nuclear series characterizes trace norm
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. T is trace class iff a positive-integer-indexed operator series T=Σ_j(x↦⟨x,u_j⟩v_j) converges in operator norm with Σ_j||u_j||||v_j||<∞. The trace norm is the infimum of these sums, attained after explicitly reindexing the SVD series by the positive integers.
items.strategy: SVD yields a nuclear series attaining Σs_j. Conversely summable rank-one norms give operator-norm convergence and compactness. For the first n singular pairs expand Σ_{k≤n}⟨Te_k,f_k⟩ through any nuclear series; absolute convergence, finite Cauchy–Schwarz and Bessel bound it by Σ||u_j||||v_j||. Supremum in n gives trace class and the norm infimum.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is inherited from SVD, Fourier expansion, and compact norm closure; given nuclear sequences require no additional selection.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp — Chapter II, §5, Proposition 2.9

items.title: Trace class is a two sided Banach operator ideal
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Trace-class operators are Banach in ||·||_1, satisfy ||T||≤||T||_1, and obey ||ATB||_1≤||A||||T||_1||B||.
items.strategy: Rank-one norms and the nuclear infimum give operator norm, triangle, and ideal bounds, with compactness established in each converse use by finite-rank partial sums and the norm-limit theorem. For a trace-norm Cauchy sequence choose a subsequence with summable differences and near-minimizing nuclear representations, flatten them to build a compact operator-norm limit, and prove trace-norm convergence; then recover the whole sequence.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega supplies the needed countable selections of a fast subsequence and near-minimizing nuclear series; no stronger use occurs.

items.title: Trace of a trace class operator
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For trace-class T and a specified Hilbert basis E, define tr_E(T)=Σ_{e∈E}⟨Te,e⟩ by the arbitrary-index finite-subset net. The sum is absolutely convergent; the next theorem proves basis independence.
items.strategy: Factor T=AB with two HS operators. For finite F, Cauchy–Schwarz bounds Σ_F|⟨ABe,e⟩| by the product of finite HS sums for B and A*, hence uniformly by their HS norms. This proves absolute summability before the basis-relative definition and does not use the following theorem forward.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is inherited from trace factorization and basis-independent Hilbert–Schmidt summation; the basis is supplied as data, not asserted to exist.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp — Chapter II, §5, Proposition 2.8

items.title: Trace is absolutely convergent and basis independent
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every trace-class T there is a unique scalar, denoted tr(T), equal to the absolutely convergent sum Σ_j⟨v_j,u_j⟩ for every nuclear representation Tx=Σ_j⟨x,u_j⟩v_j with Σ_j||u_j||||v_j||<∞. This defines tr(T) without assuming that the ambient Hilbert space has a Hilbert basis. For every supplied Hilbert basis E, tr_E(T)=tr(T). The resulting trace is linear and |tr(T)|≤||T||_1.
items.strategy: A nuclear representation R=(u_j,v_j) gives an absolutely convergent scalar tau_R=Σ_j⟨v_j,u_j⟩ because |⟨v_j,u_j⟩|≤||u_j||||v_j||. To compare two representations R and R', let K be the closed span of the union of their four countable support families {u_j,v_j,u'_j,v'_j}. Pad a finite or empty family by zeros and explicitly enumerate all finite combinations over Q in the real case and over Q(i) in the complex case, including the constant zero sequence when K={0}; this is a supplied countable dense sequence in K. The separable-Hilbert supplier therefore constructs a finite or countable Hilbert basis F of K without choosing a basis of the ambient space. Both representations show that T maps K into K and vanishes on K-perp. For either representation, Bessel and Cauchy–Schwarz give Σ_jΣ_{f in F}|⟨f,u_j⟩⟨v_j,f⟩|≤Σ_j||u_j||||v_j||, so absolute convergence permits interchange; first-variable-linear Parseval in K gives Σ_{f in F}⟨Tf,f⟩=Σ_j⟨v_j,u_j⟩. Applying this to R and R' proves tau_R=tau_R'. Nuclear existence then gives a unique scalar tr(T). For any supplied ambient Hilbert basis E, the same absolutely convergent double-sum calculation and Parseval in H give tr_E(T)=Σ_j⟨v_j,u_j⟩=tr(T); no existence of E is asserted. The estimate |tr(T)|≤Σ_j||u_j||||v_j|| for every representation and the nuclear infimum give |tr(T)|≤||T||_1. Finally, concatenate chosen nuclear representations of S and T after multiplying the v-vectors by the two scalars; representation independence then proves tr(aS+bT)=a tr(S)+b tr(T).
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is inherited from nuclear characterization and arbitrary-index Parseval. The comparison uses only the deterministically generated countable dense sequence in the closed span of two supplied nuclear supports; the separable-Hilbert supplier constructs its basis from that sequence. No Hilbert basis of the possibly nonseparable ambient space, no simultaneous choice of representations, and no full AC are used.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp — Chapter II, §5, Proposition 2.8

items.title: Cyclicity of the trace
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If T is trace class and S bounded, ST and TS are trace class and tr(ST)=tr(TS). If A,B are Hilbert–Schmidt of compatible types, tr(AB)=tr(BA).
items.strategy: For rank-one R(x)=⟨x,u⟩v, the nuclear trace formula gives tr(SR)=⟨Sv,u⟩=⟨v,S*u⟩=tr(RS). Pass from finite rank to T using trace-norm density, the ideal estimate, and |tr|≤||·||_1. For two HS factors use the absolutely convergent double matrix-coefficient sum.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is inherited from trace-norm density and factorization; no series is rearranged before absolute convergence.

items.title: Trace of a positive operator is the sum of its eigenvalues
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If T is self-adjoint, positive and trace class, then tr(T)=sum_n lambda_n=||T||_1 for its positive eigenvalues with multiplicity. This is the positive compact self-adjoint case only, not Lidskii for arbitrary trace-class operators.
items.strategy: Scaffold repair (Step 3b): self-adjointness is required (positivity alone does not give it over a real Hilbert space). Use |T|=T by uniqueness of the positive square root, so the singular values are the positive eigenvalues; the support-only SVD series is nuclear with sum ||T||_1 and the nuclear trace formula gives tr(T)=sum lambda_n.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is inherited from the support SVD and nuclear trace formula. No Hilbert basis of the possibly nonseparable kernel and no full AC is used.

title: Compact Self Adjoint Hilbert Schmidt and Trace Class Operators — Examples

items.title: Diagonal Schatten class criteria on ell two
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For Te_n=d_ne_n on ℓ²(N), T is bounded iff d∈ℓ∞, compact iff d_n→0, Hilbert–Schmidt iff Σ|d_n|²<∞, and trace class iff Σ|d_n|<∞. In the trace-class case tr(T)=Σd_n.
items.strategy: Compute ||T||=sup|d_n|. Coordinate truncations prove compactness if d_n→0, and compactness of {Te_n} proves the converse. Since |T| is diagonal with entries |d_n|, the standard basis computes HS norm, trace norm, and trace.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is inherited from the singular-value and trace interfaces; the standard basis is explicit.

items.title: Volterra operator is Hilbert Schmidt and quasinilpotent
items.statement: Assume AC. On L²[0,1], Vf(x)=∫_0^x f(t)dt is Hilbert–Schmidt with ||V||_HS²=1/2, is compact, has no nonzero eigenvalue, and has spectrum {0}.
items.strategy: Its kernel 1_{0≤t≤x} has L² norm squared 1/2, so the imported kernel theorem gives HS and compactness. Iterated integration gives V^nf(x)=1/(n-1)!∫_0^x(x-t)^{n-1}f(t)dt and the explicit factorial operator-norm bound. If Vf=λf with λ≠0, divide that bound by |λ|^n and use the ratio test to show the quotient tends to zero, contradicting the eigenvector inequality. Riesz–Schauder then gives spectrum {0}. Finally compare the pairings on f=1 and g=x to prove V is not self-adjoint directly.
items.axiom_audit: Full AC is propagated from the sigma-finite kernel theorem and Riesz–Schauder.

items.title: Rank one operator adjoint norm and trace
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. With the first-variable-linear convention, T(x)=⟨x,v⟩u has T*(x)=⟨x,u⟩v, ||T||=||u||||v||, one nonzero singular value ||u||||v|| when u,v≠0, and tr(T)=⟨u,v⟩.
items.strategy: Compute the adjoint from the defining pairing. Cauchy–Schwarz gives the norm upper bound and x=v/||v|| gives equality. Compute T*T on span(v) for the singular value. The nuclear trace formula gives tr(T)=⟨u,v⟩ with the stated convention.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is inherited from SVD and trace; no new basis is selected.

items.title: Integral operator trace under a valid diagonal hypothesis
items.statement: Assume AC. Let X be a compact metric space with finite regular Borel measure and k:X×X→C continuous, Hermitian, and positive semidefinite. Then T_k on L²(X) is positive trace class and tr(T_k)=∫_Xk(x,x)dμ(x). An arbitrary L²-kernel has no defined diagonal, and continuity without positivity does not imply trace class.
items.strategy: Construct the reproducing-kernel Hilbert space H_k by quotienting the span of symbols k_x=k(·,x) by the null space of ⟨k_y,k_x⟩=k(x,y) and completing. The reproducing identity h(x)=⟨h,k_x⟩ and sup_x k(x,x)<∞ show that the inclusion J:H_k→L²(X) is bounded. Hermitian positivity gives T_k=JJ*: indeed (JJ*f)(x)=⟨f,Jk_x⟩=∫k(x,y)f(y)dμ(y) in the first-variable-linear convention. Use AC to choose a finite 1/n-net of X for each n; their union is a countable dense set D. Since ||k_x-k_y||²=k(x,x)+k(y,y)-k(x,y)-k(y,x), continuity makes x↦k_x continuous, and rational complex linear combinations of {k_d:d∈D} form a countable dense subset of H_k. The separable-Hilbert supplier therefore gives a finite or countable orthonormal basis (e_n). Countable Parseval at k_x and Tonelli now legitimately give ||J||_HS²=Σ_n||Je_n||²=∫Σ_n|e_n(x)|²dμ=∫||k_x||²dμ=∫k(x,x)dμ. Thus J and J* are Hilbert–Schmidt, so T_k is positive trace class; cyclicity yields tr(T_k)=tr(J*J)=Σ_n||Je_n||²=∫k(x,x)dμ. Continuity on compact X supplies boundedness and measurability, while the imported square-kernel theorem supplies the original integral operator's well-definedness. State explicitly that an arbitrary L² kernel has no diagonal and that continuity without positivity gives no positive factorization.
items.axiom_audit: Full AC is used by the imported sigma-finite kernel theorem and, locally, to choose one finite metric net for each n; this supplies AC_omega for completion, Parseval, Hilbert–Schmidt, and trace dependencies. The resulting RKHS basis is countable, so Tonelli is not applied to an arbitrary uncountable family and Zorn is unnecessary.

items.title: Compact does not imply Hilbert Schmidt
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. The diagonal operator Te_n=n^{-1/2}e_n on ℓ² is compact but not Hilbert–Schmidt.
items.strategy: The diagonal tends to zero, while its squared HS norm is the divergent harmonic series.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is propagated from the diagonal criterion; the witness is explicit and uses no further choice.

items.title: Hilbert Schmidt does not imply trace class
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. The diagonal operator Te_n=n^{-1}e_n on ℓ² is Hilbert–Schmidt but not trace class.
items.strategy: Its squared singular values sum as Σ1/n²<∞, while its singular values give the divergent harmonic series.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is propagated from the diagonal criterion; the witness is explicit and uses no further choice.

items.title: The unilateral shift obstructs a cyclic linear trace extension
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For the unilateral shift S on ℓ², S*S=I and SS*=I-P_0. Neither product is trace class, while S*S-SS*=P_0 is rank one with trace 1; hence no linear extension of the trace can be cyclic on this pair.
items.strategy: Compute S* on the standard basis and hence both products. I is not trace class, while P_0 is rank one of trace one. A cyclic linear extension would force its value on P_0 to be both zero and one.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is inherited from trace-class cyclicity; the shift calculation is explicit.

items.title: Schatten p classes
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For 1≤p<∞, S_p consists of compact operators with singular values in ℓ^p and norm (Σs_n^p)^{1/p}; S_1 is trace class, S_2 is Hilbert–Schmidt, and S_∞ denotes compact operators with operator norm. This is orientation only.
items.strategy: State the scale and identify p=1,2,∞. Do not develop interpolation, duality, Hölder inequalities, or allow later dependencies on this remark.
items.axiom_audit: AC_omega is inherited from singular values and endpoints; no new claim of basis existence.
